answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because dawn only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, signal is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
